question: What does each framework make easy that the other two make hard (typed state graphs, role/crew delegation, conversational group chat), and which of those abstractions is transferable to a prompt-native control plane WITHOUT importing a second orchestration runtime?
answer: LangGraph makes typed shared-state graphs easy: nodes communicate through a TypedDict/Pydantic State whose keys carry independent reducer functions, then StateGraph.compile() builds a Pregel app (checkpointer optional). CrewAI and AutoGen snapshots do not contain that reducer annotation. CrewAI makes role/crew delegation easy: Agent(role, goal, backstory) plus Process.sequential or Process.hierarchical (manager agent + manager_llm). LangGraph and AutoGen snapshots do not contain that role/goal/backstory agent contract. AutoGen/AG2 makes conversational group chat easy: GroupChatManager selects a speaker and broadcasts each utterance to all other agents. LangGraph and CrewAI snapshots do not contain that broadcast loop. Transfer onto this estate's prompt-native control plane (WFA-0044 WorkflowIR, no second orchestration runtime): typed state graphs ARE transferable as IR state_schema + reducer names + edges (cost: schema extension plus overwrite/list-concat; do not import Pregel/checkpointer). Sequential role/crew IS transferable as existing IR role nodes plus ordered stages (cost: map the three prompt fields; do not import Crew.kickoff). Conversational group chat is NOT transferable without the GroupChatManager speaker-select-and-broadcast loop (named runtime service). SUCCESS:RES-0176

claims.others_make_hard: CrewAI tasks pass string context, not per-key reducers. AutoGen group chat treats the message list as the conversation state; neither snapshot contains the LangGraph reducer annotation.

transfer_verdicts.mechanism: Named state keys with an independent merge rule per key (overwrite or list-concat / custom reducer) plus explicit node and edge topology.
transfer_verdicts.reimplementation_cost: Extend WFA-0044 WorkflowIR with a state_schema object (key -> {type, reducer}) and a conditional_edge table; implement overwrite and list-concat in the existing prompt-native runner. Do not install langgraph. Checkpointer put/get and interrupt_before stay unmapped (Pregel persistence).
transfer_verdicts.what_importing_would_do: Importing langgraph would add a Pregel superstep scheduler and checkpoint store — a second orchestration runtime.

transfer_verdicts.mechanism: Role/goal/backstory prompt triple plus an ordered task list (sequential process).
transfer_verdicts.reimplementation_cost: Map Agent.role/goal/backstory onto existing WFA-0044 IR nodes of kind=role; map sequential Task lists onto existing stage order. Do not install crewai. Process.hierarchical (_run_hierarchical_process / _create_manager_agent) is not in this transferable slice.
transfer_verdicts.what_importing_would_do: Importing Crew.kickoff would add CrewAI's process executor as a second control loop beside the prompt-native plane.

transfer_verdicts.mechanism: Speaker-selection policy over an agent roster plus broadcast of each utterance to all other agents.
transfer_verdicts.runtime_service: GroupChatManager speaker-select-and-broadcast loop: select_speaker, groupchat.append, then self.send(message, agent, request_reply=False) to every non-speaker
transfer_verdicts.reimplementation_cost: Not reimplemented. Doing so would add an in-session agent registry, nested LLM speaker-selection, and all-to-all message fan-out — a second conversation orchestration runtime, forbidden by _USER-PROMPTS.md:10727. A prompt-native plane may still sequence named speakers as ordinary stages; that is not this abstraction.
transfer_verdicts.what_importing_would_do: Importing GroupChatManager would create a second orchestration runtime inside the session.

negative_control.runtime_service: GroupChatManager speaker-select-and-broadcast loop: select_speaker, groupchat.append, then self.send(message, agent, request_reply=False) to every non-speaker
negative_control.why: The abstraction is the runtime: an agent registry plus nested speaker selection plus all-to-all fan-out. Importing it creates a second orchestration runtime.
